title: Payment API Database Overload via Unindexed Batch Query
symptoms: Postgres connection timeouts across all API clients
p99 latency spiked to 6.8s on primary read/write node
IOPS ceiling reached on primary storage volume
investigation_steps: Queried pg_stat_activity for longest running queries
Discovered full table scan query on 14M rows in ledger_transactions table
Confirmed application worker pool was NOT leaking sockets
Identified new reporting batch cron triggered on primary rather than read-replica
findings: Root cause is database engine CPU & I/O overload, NOT a connection leak in application code
Worker connection pool saturated because database server was unable to service queries fast enough
root_cause: Database CPU and I/O overload caused by unindexed analytical reporting query executing against primary database replica.
actions_taken: Added composite index on ledger_transactions(merchant_id, created_at)
Redirected reporting-worker connection string to read-only replica endpoint
resolution: Terminated blocking query, added index on ledger_transactions, and redirected analytical traffic to read replica.
verification: Database CPU dropped from 98% to 18%, p99 latency returned to 45ms, and connection pool backlog cleared immediately.
recommendations: Enforce read-replica routing for all automated reporting and reconciliation queries
engineer_feedback: Important distinction: Even though symptom was DB connection timeout, cause was DB server overload from batch query, not a worker leak.
